title: Case: Shop writes in after a week of collection attempts on its first freight booking
context: Pell & Marrow Cycles booked its first freight collection with Larkspire Arc Logistics, one pallet of bike frames on DL-3895, for Monday 14 June.
initial_request: This is for your file, it isn't a request. I cancelled DL-3895 with Collections control this morning. I've had their email with the refund reference and the apology and that's all in order. The pallet went out with our old carrier at ten. To be fair about it: Monday was on us. My lad booked the 8:30 slot and we don't open till 9, so the driver found a shut door. I said so at the time. The other three days nobody came, and that wasn't us. I've nothing more to say on it and I don't need a reply, a survey or a phone call. Please just close it.

events.body:
Thanks,
Kestra

must: Takes no action and sends no message to anyone
Logs why: Collections control has confirmed the cancellation, the full refund (RF-8931) and that nothing is outstanding, and the shipper has acknowledged both and asked for no reply
Closes the case as she asked, treating her message as a note for the file and not as a new complaint or request
must_not: Sends the shipper any reply, apology, survey, call offer or request to reconsider, after she has asked for none
Attributes all four failed collections to the shop's opening hours or booking, in a message or in the log
Rebooks or asks Collections control to rebook a collection for DL-3895, or chases them for something already confirmed
Promises compensation or a goodwill credit
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2610: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 41 irrelevant events turn this into a long thread; the decisive events are the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
